topline.text: Ofsted's leadership crisis sharpened overnight - a snap NEU poll found 98% no confidence in chief inspector Sir Martyn Oliver, and governors separately called report-card inspections 'brutal'.
topline.action: NEU wants Oliver to go, inspections paused, and an urgent framework review - worth watching before your next inspection window.

topline.text: Locally: Sheffield's finance committee votes Monday on £602k funding for a Firth Park Academy expansion adding three new SEND rooms alongside 30 extra Year 7 places.
From tomorrow (16 Oct), employers can start consulting staff on pay policies for the 3.5% 2026-27 teacher pay award - though the Pay Order itself still has to clear Parliament.

diary.text: Employers in England can begin consulting staff on updated pay policies for the 2026-27 teacher pay award.
Sheffield City Council finance and performance committee votes on £602k funding for the Firth Park Academy SEND-places expansion.

items.body: A snap poll of almost 7,000 NEU members in English state schools, run overnight 12-13 October, found 98% have no confidence in Ofsted's current leadership and 96% back an immediate pause on inspections. General secretary Daniel Kebede said Oliver 'has lost the confidence of the profession and it is time for him to go'.

The National Governance Association's annual survey found governors describing report-card inspections as 'brutal', with some school leadership teams 'breaking down routinely' under the pressure - despite 71% saying their last inspection gave a fair and accurate picture, up only 3 points on 2022's record low.
ASCL's council passed its own no-confidence vote in Ofsted's leadership last week over unaddressed workload and wellbeing concerns.

items.lede: Firth Park Academy set for SEND-focused expansion.
items.body: Sheffield's finance and performance committee meets Monday 19 October to approve passing £602,000 of government funding to Lift Schools, part of a £701,312 scheme adding three SEND rooms, refurbished creative-arts space and upgraded science labs - raising Firth Park's admission number from 240 to 270 to help meet a projected secondary-places shortfall in 2027/28 and 2028/29.

items.lede: Pay policy consultations open from tomorrow.
items.body: From 16 October, employers can consult staff on pay policies reflecting the accepted 3.5% uplift for 2026-27 (5% at the bottom of the unqualified range), backdated to 1 September. The Pay Order itself still has to clear its parliamentary praying period before arrears follow - worth flagging to business managers as a timing uncertainty.
